title: Apostolic Lent; terms confused with Divine; Ecclesiastical customs by consent
source_text: XIII. Apostolicae vero traditiones ab iis proprie dicuntur, quae ab Apostolis praecepta & instituta opinantur, quamvis eorum mentio nulla fiat in scriptis Apostolicis. Ad quas traditiones referunt jejunium quod vocant Quadragesimae, quod ab Apostolis institutum autumant. Et tamen saepe has voces contundunt, traditiones Divinas vocantes ea, quae non Christus ipse, sed Apostoli tantum instituisse putantur: quoniam quae sunt ab iis instituta non sine divini Spiritus afflatu instituerunt. Et vicissim quae ad Christum referunt, traditiones quoque Apostolicas vocant, quoniam eorum quae Christus docuit nihil ad nos pervenit, nisi per Apostolorum scripta & praedicationem. Ecclesiasticae vero traditiones ab iis vocantur quaedam consuetudines antiquae, vel a Praelatis, vel a populis inchoatae, quae paulatim tacito populorum consensu vim legis obtinuerunt.
pass_a_gloss: But Apostolic traditions are properly so called by them which they think were commanded and instituted by the Apostles, although no mention of them is made in the Apostolic writings. To these traditions they refer the fast they call Quadragesima (Lent), which they claim was instituted by the Apostles. And yet they often confuse these words, calling Divine traditions those which not Christ himself but only the Apostles are thought to have instituted — because what was instituted by them was not without the breath of the divine Spirit. And conversely what they refer to Christ they also call Apostolic traditions, because nothing of what Christ taught has come to us except through the Apostles' writings and preaching. But Ecclesiastical traditions are called by them certain ancient customs, begun either by prelates or by peoples, which little by little by the tacit consent of the peoples obtained the force of law.
pass_b_english: Apostolic traditions, in the proper sense, are commands and institutes they ascribe to the Apostles even when the Apostolic writings are silent.
Under that head they place the Quadragesima (Lent) fast, which they claim the Apostles founded.

Often they blur the labels: what only the Apostles (not Christ) instituted they still call Divine, because those institutes came with the Spirit's breath; and what they tie to Christ they also call Apostolic, since nothing of Christ's teaching reaches us except through Apostolic writing and preaching.
Ecclesiastical traditions are old customs begun by prelates or peoples that, by gradual tacit consent, took on the force of law.

lemmas.gloss: by the tacit consent of the peoples

choices.why: Standing Roman example of Apostolic tradition; keep both names once.
Spirit's breath behind Apostolic institutes they elevate toward Divine.
